name: Battle of Königgrätz

phases.title: The armies take position either side of the river
phases.text: The Prussians took their position west of the Bystřice river. The Austrian infantry stood partly fortified, with artillery behind it and cavalry in the rear, and the Saxons on the Austrian left.

phases.title: Austrian guns pin down the Prussian right
phases.text: The Austrian artillery opened fire on the Prussian right under Herwarth von Bittenfeld. The Saxons fell back in good order and fired on the advancing Prussians from higher ground. Around 10 am the advance guard of seven battalions was pulled back to the river.

phases.title: The 7th Division advances into the Swiepwald
phases.text: The Prussian centre went into the Swiepwald, where two Austrian corps met it. The First Army was ordered across the river to support the 7th Division, and Austrian artillery cut down the Prussians as they came out of the smoke.

phases.title: Pöckh's charge is raked by flanking fire
phases.text: The Austrian centre moved to flank the 7th Division, and Pöckh's infantry charge forced it back to the outskirts of the forest. Flanking fire from the 8th Division then raked his battalion and killed its commander.

phases.title: The Second Army reaches the field
phases.text: Crown Prince Frederick William arrived with the main bulk of the Second Army and hit the Austrian right flank as it retired from the Swiepwald. The 1st Guard came with it.

phases.title: The Austrian line breaks at Chlum and Probluz
phases.text: The Second Army broke through the Austrian lines and took Chlum behind the centre, and the 1st Guard reached the Austrian artillery. On the other side the Army of the Elbe broke through the Austrian left and seized Probluz.

phases.title: Austrian cavalry cover the retreat
phases.text: Benedek ordered a general retreat and a series of cavalry countercharges to back up his artillery and cover it. The cavalry kept the bridges over the Elbe open, at a cost of 2,000 men and almost as many horses.

note: The accounts put the Prussians west of the Bystřice river, the Saxons on the Austrian left, the 7th Division in the Prussian centre and Chlum behind the Austrian centre; they do not give compass directions or exact positions, so the plan is schematic. Which Prussian formation stood left or right of the others, and where the Austrian right stood before the Second Army came, is placed by judgement. The Second Army is drawn arriving on the Austrian right, as the accounts say it struck that flank.
